frame.godot_axes: X = x, Y = z (up), Z = y; the camera sits at +Z (south) looking north

camera.law: screen_x = ppm*x ; screen_y = ppm*sin(a)*y - ppm*cos(a)*z ; zero yaw (x screen-right, +y toward camera = screen-down)
camera.godot_camera: Camera3D orthographic, keep_aspect KEEP_HEIGHT, size = viewport_rows / ppm, rotation_degrees = (-pitch, 0, 0), placed at target + D*(0, sin(pitch), cos(pitch)) in Godot axes (X = x, Y = up, Z = y)

provenance.csv_note: the CSV is the level-frame source (sm1/survivalworld_a.map); the pack's sg1 rows are its arena-centred image and are what this layout uses
provenance.scatter_model_basis_verbatim: SIM-ROLLED BOX -- each axis rolled INDEPENDENTLY about the body's own emitter anchor: sx = anchor_x + U(-h, +h), sy = anchor_y + U(-h, +h), with h = placement_extents_m (the half-width, per axis; the magnitude stays in that typed field and is deliberately not repeated here). NOT A DISC: the box's corner sits 1.414 x h from the anchor, so a loader drawing an h-radius circle draws the wrong region and rejects bodies the sim placed correctly.

scatter.model: DISC: polar, theta = 2 pi u1, rho = 8 u2 (ScatterLaw.POLAR_UNIFORM_RHO, the default)

law_provenance.runtime: the arena runtime matches it bit for bit (drax G3)
law_provenance.confirmed_by: KC2 conductor via the C-9 conductor (lane BX ruling, 2026-10-03)

scatter.⚑ pack_erratum: The pack's arena.json presentation_defaults.scatter_model describes a per-axis BOX; that prose is stale (the oracle rolls the polar disc above). Logged as a pack erratum for star-lord. Layout v1 had built its floor on the box (4,670.8 m2); v2 uses the disc hull, as ruled.

stair._ruling: R-C9-145 (Matt) + R-C9-148 (Matt, from the walk film: 'the stairs seem to be below the sea cave which doesnt make alot of sense'): the cave sits in the MAIN south cliff face under p03's patch with a ledge at sea level; a straight stair, 3.0 m wide, climbs FROM that ledge UP the face to a top landing flush with the floor edge at p03's patch; open on the sea side; its run angles across the face (the 'aligned to centre' rule is dropped by R-C9-148); climbers turn toward the centre on the landing

top_landing.north_edge: follows the floor boundary vertex-for-vertex (flush, same z as the floor) at p03's patch

flight.polygon_order: top wall-side, top sea-side, foot sea-side, foot wall-side
flight.walk_model: a REAL RAMP: one plane under the step nosings, the same slope as the treads' pitch line; the steps are a visual on it. Godot CharacterBody3D floor_max_angle default 45 deg > the slope, so a body walks it without a step-up solver
flight.stair_rule_check: 2R + T = 0.600 m (the comfortable band is 0.60-0.65 m)

bottom_landing.note: the rock ledge at sea level in front of the cave; the flight's foot stands on it

stair.open_side: SOUTH (the sea side): no wall, no rail
stair.wall_side: NORTH: the main cliff face (stair_wall_rock fills the face between the straight flight and the curved lip)
stair.placement: OUTSIDE the floor polygon (it climbs the cliff face). The sim never reads it; it is the visible delivery path from the cave to the p03 patch.
